name: Leyla
presentingProblem: I turned down a promotion at work last month. It would have meant presenting to the team every week. I just… couldn't. I think I'm too shy. My sister told me I should talk to someone.
backstory: Leyla is a 31-year-old accountant at a mid-sized firm in Ankara. She is technically excellent at her work and has been quietly promoted twice for the quality of her analyses, but each time the role has expanded toward visibility she has withdrawn or stepped sideways. She grew up in a traditional Turkish family where her mother praised her for being 'mütevazı' (modest) and warned that visible girls attract 'nazar' — the evil eye — and gossip. Her father teased her gently for blushing, which she remembers vividly. She has two close friends from university whom she sees rarely. She has never been in a romantic relationship; she once liked a colleague but could not bring herself to reply to his messages and he eventually stopped writing. She lives alone and tells her family she is 'too busy with work' to date. In sessions she sits with her hands in her lap, gives short answers, and apologizes often for 'not being interesting.'

coreBeliefs: If people really knew me, they would reject me
I am fundamentally different from other people in a bad way
intermediateBeliefs: It's safer to say nothing than to risk saying something foolish
If I make myself small, people won't see what's wrong with me
automaticThoughts: I shouldn't have said that — that was stupid
She's just being polite, she actually finds me boring
If I take the promotion they'll see I don't really belong
I'm wasting your time today, you must have more interesting clients
triggers: Direct questions about her feelings (she goes silent)
Discussion of the promotion she turned down
Being asked about romantic or family expectations
defenses: Avoidance of feared situations (presentations, dating, conflict)
Pre-emptive self-deprecation ('I'm probably not explaining this well')
Minimal disclosure — answers in one or two words when anxious
Apologizing for taking up space in the conversation
values: Not being a burden to others
Honesty with the few people she trusts
Quiet, private moments with books and her cat
